title: Two extremes: Christ and the Antichrist
source_text: Ἐπεὶ δὲ καὶ τὰ περὶ τοῦ καλουμένου ἀντιχρίστου παραῤῥιπτεῖ ὁ Κέλσος. ουτε τὰ ἐν τῷ Δανιὴλ οὔτε τὰ παρὰ τῷ Παύλῳ ἀναγνοὺς περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰρημένα οὔτε τὰ ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος προφητευθέντα περὶ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, ὀλίγα καὶ περὶ τούτου λεκτέον. ὅτι „ὥσπερ οὐχ ὅμοια πρόσωπα προσώποις. οὕτως οὐδὲ αἱ καρδίαι ὅμοιαι ταῖς καρδίαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων.“ δῆλον ὅτι εἶεν ἂν ἐν „ταῖς καρδίαις τῶν ἀνθρώπων“ διαφοραὶ καὶ τῶν πρὸς τὸ καλὸν νενευκότων, οὐκ ἐπ᾿ ἴσης καὶ παραπλησίως ἀλλήλοις πάντων τυπωθέντων καὶ μορφωθέντων πρὸς αὐτὸ, καὶ τῶν δι᾿ ἀμέλειαν τοῦ καλοῦ ἐπὶ τὰ ἐναντία ᾀττόντων· καὶ ἐν τούτοις γὰρ ἐν οἷς μέν ἐστι σφόδρα κεχυμένη ἡ κακία ἐν οἷς δ᾿ ἐπ᾿ ἔλαττον· τί οὖν ἄτοπον δύο, ἵν᾿ οὕτως ὀνομάσω, ἀκρότητας. τὴν μὲν τοῦ καλοῦ τὴν δὲ τοῦ ἐναντίου, ἐν ἀνθρώποις γίνεσθαι, ὥστε τὴν μὲν τοῦ καλοῦ ἀκρότητα εἶναι ἐν τῷ κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν νοουμένῳ ἀνθρώπῳ, ἀφ᾿ ου ἡ τοσαύτη ἔῤῥευσε τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπιστροφὴ καὶ θεραπεία καὶ βελτίωσις, τὴν δὲ τοῦ ἐναντίου ἐν τῷ κατὰ τὸν ὀνομαζόμενον ἀντίχριστον; πάντα δὲ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ προγνώσει ἐκπεριλαβὼν ὁ θεὸς καὶ ἰδὼν τὰ περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τούτων ἐβουλήθη περὶ τούτων γνωρίσαι διὰ τῶν προφητῶν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἵνα οἱ συνιέντες τῶν λόγων αὐτῶν οἰκειωθῶσι μὲν τῷ κρείττονι. φυλάξωνται δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐναντίου. ἐχρῆν δὲ τὸν μὲν ἕτερον τῶν ἄκρων καὶ βέλτιστον υἱὸν ἀναγορεύεσθαι τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὴν ὑπεροχὴν, τὸν δὲ τούτῳ κατὰ διάμετρον ἐναντίον υἱὸν τοῦ πονηροῦ δαίμονος καὶ Σατανᾶ καὶ διαβόλου. εἶτ᾿ ἐπεὶ τότε μάλιστα τὸ φαῦλον ἐν τῇ χύσει τῆς κακίας καὶ τῇ ἀκρότητι αὐτῆς εἶναι χαρακτηρίζεται, ὅτε ὑποκρίνεται τὸ κρεῖττον, διὰ τοῦτο περὶ τὸν χείρονα γίνεται ἐκ συνεργίας τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ διαβόλου σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα καὶ δυνάμεις ψεύδους. ὑπὲρ γὰρ τὰς εἰς τοὺς γόητας γινομένας ἀπὸ δαιμόνων συνεργίας πρὸς τὰ φαυλότατα τῶν ἀνθρώπους ἀπατώντων γίνεται συνεργία ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐπὶ ἀπάτῃ τοῦ γένους τῶν ἀνθρώπων. Λέγει δὲ ὁ Παῦλος περὶ τούτου τοῦ καλουμένου ἀντιχρίστου διδάσκων καὶ παριστὰς μετά τινος ἐπικρύψεως, τίνα τρόπον ἐπιδημήσει καὶ πότε τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ διὰ τί· καὶ ὅρα εἰ μὴ σεμνότατα περὶ τούτων ὁ Παῦλος ἐκτίθεται καὶ οὐκ ἀξίως χλεύης τινὸς κἂν ἐλαχίστης·
pass_a_gloss: Since Celsus also throws in by the way (παραρρίπτω) the things about the so-called antichrist (ἀντίχριστος), having read (ἀναγιγνώσκω) neither the things in Daniel nor the things in Paul said about him nor the things prophesied (προφητεύω) by the Saviour in the Gospels about his coming (παρουσία), a few things must be said (λεκτέον) about this also. That 'as faces (πρόσωπα) are not like (ὅμοια) faces, so neither are the hearts (καρδίαι) like the hearts of men'; it is clear that there would be in 'the hearts of men' differences (διαφοραί) both of those having inclined (νεύω) toward the good (τὸ καλόν), not all having been stamped (τυπόω) and formed (μορφόω) toward it equally (ἐπ᾿ ἴσης) and similarly to one another, and of those through neglect (ἀμέλεια) of the good rushing (ᾄττω) to the opposites; for in these also, in some wickedness is greatly poured out (χέω), in others less. What then absurd (ἄτοπον) that two, that I may so name them, extremes (ἀκρότης), one of the good, the other of the opposite, come to be among men, so that the extreme of the good is in the man (ἄνθρωπος) understood (νοέω) in the case of Jesus (κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν), from whom so great conversion (ἐπιστροφή) and healing (θεραπεία) and improvement (βελτίωσις) flowed (ῥέω) to the race (γένος) of men, and that of the opposite in the one [understood] in the case of the one named antichrist? God, having embraced (ἐκπεριλαμβάνω) all things by his foreknowledge (πρόγνωσις) and having seen the things about both these, willed (βούλομαι) to make known (γνωρίζω) about them through the prophets to men, that those understanding (συνίημι) their words may be made akin (οἰκειόω) to the better (κρεῖττον) and guard (φυλάσσομαι) against the opposite. And it was needful that the one of the extremes and best (βέλτιστος) be proclaimed (ἀναγορεύω) Son of God because of his pre-eminence (ὑπεροχή), and the one diametrically (κατὰ διάμετρον) opposite to him son of the evil daemon and Satanas and devil. Then, since the base (τὸ φαῦλον) is characterised (χαρακτηρίζω) as being most in the outpouring (χύσις) of wickedness and its extreme then, when it feigns (ὑποκρίνομαι) the better, because of this there come about the worse one (χείρων), from the co-working (συνεργία) of his father the devil, signs (σημεῖα) and wonders (τέρατα) and powers (δυνάμεις) of falsehood (ψεῦδος). For beyond the co-workings from daemons happening to sorcerers (γόητες) deceiving (ἀπατάω) men to the basest things, there is a co-working from the devil himself for deceit (ἀπάτη) of the race of men. And Paul speaks about this so-called antichrist, teaching and presenting (παρίστημι) with some concealment (ἐπίκρυψις) in what way he will come to dwell (ἐπιδημέω) and when among the race of men and why; and see whether Paul does not set out (ἐκτίθεμαι) these things most solemnly (σεμνότατα) and not worthy of mockery (χλεύη), even the least.
pass_b_english: Since Celsus also tosses in, in passing, what is said about the one called Antichrist, though he has not read what is said of him in Daniel (Daniel 8:23–25) or in Paul (2 Thessalonians 2:3–12), or what the Saviour prophesied in the Gospels about his coming (Matthew 24:23–26), we must say a little about this too. Since “just as faces are not like faces, so neither are hearts like the hearts of men” (Proverbs 27:19), it is clear that there would be differences in “the hearts of men” both among those who have inclined toward the good, since they have not all been stamped and shaped toward it equally and alike, and among those who through neglect of the good rush toward the opposite. For among these also wickedness is poured out in great measure in some, and in others to a lesser degree.

What is absurd, then, in there being among men two extremes, if I may so call them, one of good and the other of its opposite, so that the extreme of good is in the man discerned in Jesus, from whom so great a conversion, healing and betterment flowed to the human race, and the extreme of the opposite is in the man discerned in the one called Antichrist? God, who has embraced all things in his foreknowledge and has seen what concerns both of these, willed to make these things known to men through the prophets, so that those who understand their words might be drawn close to the better and guard themselves against the opposite.

It was fitting that one of the two extremes, the best, should be proclaimed Son of God because of his surpassing excellence, and the one diametrically opposite to him the son of the evil demon, Satan, the devil. Then, since evil is most clearly marked as being at the outpouring of wickedness and at its height when it plays the part of the better, for this reason signs and wonders and powers of falsehood attend the worse one, through the help of his father the devil (2 Thessalonians 2:9). For beyond the help that demons give to sorcerers, who deceive men for the basest ends, there comes help from the devil himself for deceiving the human race.

Paul speaks about this one called Antichrist (2 Thessalonians 2:3–12), teaching and showing, with a certain reserve, in what way he will come among the human race, and when, and why. And see whether Paul does not set these things out with the greatest dignity, in a way that deserves not even the slightest mockery.

choices.choice: The chapter ends with a colon in the Greek: the quotation of 2 Thessalonians 2:1–12 that Paul ‘speaks’ follows at the start of 6.46. Inline citations in the first sentence mark the passages Origen names and quotes in 6.46 (Daniel 8:23–25 and 9:27; 2 Thessalonians 2:1–12); for the Saviour’s prophecy of false christs see Matthew 24:23–26 (compare Mark 13:21–22). Proverbs 27:19 is quoted from the Septuagint (ὥσπερ οὐχ ὅμοια πρόσωπα προσώποις, οὕτως οὐδὲ αἱ καρδίαι τῶν ἀνθρώπων); the Hebrew and English Bibles read differently (‘as in water face answers to face’); the verse number is the same. Origen’s form adds ὅμοιαι ταῖς καρδίαις. τῷ κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν νοουμένῳ ἀνθρώπῳ is rendered ‘the man discerned in Jesus’ (νοούμενος, ‘understood, discerned’; ‘understood in Jesus’ read as a calque): Origen means the human being, or humanity, of Jesus, as distinct from the divine Word; the parallel phrase for the Antichrist is elliptical and is filled out as ‘the man discerned in the one called Antichrist’. σφόδρα κεχυμένη and ἐν τῇ χύσει: ‘poured out in great measure’, ‘the outpouring’. πονηροῦ δαίμονος καὶ Σατανᾶ καὶ διαβόλου names one being: ‘the evil demon, Satan, the devil’. συνεργία is rendered ‘help’ in both places. ‘Signs and wonders and powers of falsehood’ is the wording of 2 Thessalonians 2:9. ‘His father the devil’ may echo John 8:44; left uncited inline as uncertain. δαίμων in Origen’s voice is rendered ‘demon’. ‘Son of God’ is capitalised for Christ; ‘son of the evil demon’ is not.
'poured out in full flood' -> 'poured out in great measure' (σφόδρα κεχυμένη; stock image removed)
'the man understood in Jesus' / 'in the one called Antichrist' -> 'the man discerned in ...' (calque)
'willed to make it known' -> 'willed to make these things known' (περὶ τούτων γνωρίσαι)
'son of the evil demon, of Satan and the devil' -> 'son of the evil demon, Satan, the devil' (one being, not two)
'evil shows itself to be in the full flood of wickedness' -> 'evil is most clearly marked as being at the outpouring of wickedness' (χαρακτηρίζεται, χύσις)
'through the working together of' -> 'through the help of' (συνεργία, same word as the next sentence's 'help')
'in words that deserve no mockery at all, not even the least' -> 'in a way that deserves not even the slightest mockery'
checked: Daniel 8:23-25 (quoted in 6.46), 2 Thessalonians 2:3-12 and 2:9, Matthew 24:23-26, Proverbs 27:19 (LXX wording, same verse number)
final colon became a full stop; 6.46 opens 'He speaks as follows:', so the quotation is still introduced
